brief:
A modeling reference sheet (turnaround) for ONE low-poly 3D game asset: a chunky cartoon kid skater named Marlo standing on a skateboard, the player character of a sunny skatepark game (an original character).

Canvas and layout, keep exactly:
- 1536 x 1024 landscape image, a 2 x 2 grid of four equal panels.
- Top-left panel: FRONT view. Top-right: RIGHT side view. Bottom-left: BACK view. Bottom-right: TOP view (looking straight down).
- Orthographic cameras (no perspective), the same scale in every panel, the figure centred in each panel and standing on the same invisible ground line in the three side views.
- Every view sits whole inside its panel with a clear margin of background all round (at least a tenth of the panel): nothing touches or crosses a panel edge, including the board's nose and tail.
- Each side view is exactly frontal to its side: no other face of the figure shows in it.
- The skater stands SIDEWAYS on the board, as skaters do: the board's long axis runs left-right under the feet in the FRONT view.
- The four panels show the SAME figure, only turned: FRONT: the skater's chest and face towards the camera, the board seen from its long side, running left-right across the panel, its nose at the RIGHT, the left foot on the nose end (image right) and the right foot on the tail end (image left). RIGHT: the camera has walked round to the side that was on the RIGHT of the image in the front view, so we look at the board's NOSE end-on (the board is a narrow upright shape under the feet, only as wide as the board, NOT a copy of the front view), and the skater is seen in profile, chest and face pointing to the LEFT edge of the image, one leg hiding the other. BACK: seen from behind (the back of the hoodie and the beanie, the board's long side again, its nose now at the LEFT). TOP: seen from straight above, looking down: the board a long rounded rectangle running left-right with its nose at the RIGHT, the beanie top in the middle, the shoulders running left-right along the board, the chest towards the BOTTOM edge of the image.
- One flat, uniform, mid grey background (#9a9a9a) everywhere: no floor, no cast shadow, no gradient, no vignette, no frame lines, no text, no labels, no logos.

The figure (identical in all four views), 1.65 m tall from the ground to the top of the beanie:
- Skateboard: a flat deck 0.90 m long, 0.26 m wide, 0.04 m thick, its top 0.15 m above the ground, nose and tail kicked up a little at the ends; two steel trucks under it with four chunky cream wheels 0.10 m across, 0.30 m in from each end.
- Shoes: big chunky white sneakers 0.28 m long, standing across the board (pointing towards the camera in the front view), one near each end of the board, 0.52 m apart.
- Legs: navy-blue jeans, thick and straight, knees slightly bent, the feet apart so the legs make a wide upside-down V in the front view; hips at 0.80 m.
- Torso: a boxy red-orange hoodie 0.44 m wide at the shoulders (left-right in the front view), 0.26 m deep, from the hips to the shoulders at 1.25 m, with a hood lying on the back and a front pocket.
- Arms: hoodie sleeves hanging a little out from the body, relaxed, ending in chunky tan hands at hip height.
- Head: a big blocky head 0.30 m wide with tan skin, two dot eyes, a small nose, facing the camera in the front view; a yellow beanie hat with a folded rim covering the top of the head, up to 1.65 m.

Style, keep exactly:
- A clean low-poly 3D model render: faceted, flat-shaded faces, hard straight edges, big readable chunky shapes, about 700 triangles worth of detail. No smooth organic surfaces, no tiny details, no texture noise, no grain, no laces, no logos, no text.
- Flat colour areas only, ONLY these colours: hoodie red-orange #df3e23 (shade #b4202a); beanie yellow #ffd541 (shade #f9a31b); jeans blue #285cc4 (shade #143464); skin tan #dba463 (shade #bb7547); shoes white #dae0ea (shade #b3b9d1); deck underside and edges magenta #bc4a9b (shade #793a80); grip tape on the deck top near-black #333941; trucks steel #8b93af; wheels cream #fef3c0; eyes #141013.
- Soft, even light from the upper left, so each face reads as one flat tone; no specular highlights, no ambient occlusion blur.
